videos.description:
For a free month of Wispr Flow Pro: ref.wisprflow.ai/ali_shorts

I run an online business school, and a big chunk of my week is replying to students on Slack.

That used to be an hour of context switching and typing, but now, I just talk into my computer.

One of our students was struggling to drive sales from her Instagram content, so instead of typing I hit the Wispr Flow shortcut and replied her within a few seconds, instead of a few minutes.

It’s voice to text for pretty much any app. It strips out the ums and errs, handles capitalisation, and it even matches tone, so if you type in all lowercase in WhatsApp, that's how your dictated message comes out. No accidental business emails in the group chat.

I barely type anything on my computer anymore.

videos.title: Rick Rubin: Your Whole Personality Is NOT True
videos.description:
Rick Rubin says the biggest block to your creativity isn't a lack of talent. It's caring what other people will think of the thing you made.

In this clip, Rick Rubin and Jay Shetty talk about why the artists who last are the ones who stopped trying to guess what the audience wants, including the eight years Rick spent refusing a book deal because every publisher was picturing a different book.

Rick opens up about telling Johnny Cash to sing a love song to God instead of a woman, why he moved a whole band into a mansion instead of a studio, and the difference between procrastination and the kind of distraction that actually solves the problem for you.

Learn about the habit he practices the second he wakes up, why moving your body too soon erases what your subconscious just told you, and why comparing two pieces of art makes about as much sense as comparing two diary entries.

JAY'S DAILY WISDOM DELIVERED STRAIGHT TO YOUR INBOX
Join 900,000+ readers discovering how small daily shifts create big life change with my free newsletter. Subscribe https://news.jayshetty.me/subscribe

videos.title: How to Improve Motivation & Overcome Procrastination | Dr. Masud Husain
videos.description:
Dr. Masud Husain is a Professor of Neurology & Cognitive Neuroscience at the University of Oxford and a leading expert on the science of motivation, apathy, and neurological diseases. We discuss how dopamine and specific brain circuits shape motivation, including how the brain weighs the trade-off between effort vs reward when deciding what goals to pursue. Dr. Husain also explains practical tools to increase motivation, reduce distractions, and make it easier to start and maintain goal pursuit. We also discuss dementia, Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s disease, including new insights into cognitive resilience and factors that help protect against age-related cognitive decline.
